newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss watchmakers clock up strong first half.
newsitem.headline: Swiss watchmakers clock up strong first half.

text.p: Swiss watchmakers celebrated a surge in earnings Friday as Ste Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie and TAG Heuer International SA reported higher first-half results.

Switzerland's biggest watchmaker, SMH, whose brands include Swatch watches, said sales in the first half of 1997 rose 7 percent to 1.414 billion Swiss francs ($930.1 million). Group operating profit surged 32 percent to 162 million francs ($106.5 million).
TAG Heuer said 1997 first-half sales rose 6.6 percent to 226.2 million ($150 million), and first-half net income was up 60.4 percent at 38.7 million francs ($25.5 million).
"I think both are on the right path. The fundamental sentiment is turning positive for the watch industry," said Eric Steinhauser, equity analyst at UBS.
The improvements were helped by the firmer dollar and better demand in some key European markets, analysts said.

SMH produces a number of brands besides Swatch, including luxury Blancpain as well as somewhat less expensive Omega and Rado. It said that stronger sales in June and July were led by its higher priced watches.
